story.title: Anthropic rival says companies can (mostly) skip the pricey models

facts.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said on Monday that his company has "never advocated for a ban on open-weights models," an attempt to beat back criticism emerging across the tech industry that the AI lab is trying to exert excessive control over the future of artificial intelligence.
Chief rival OpenAI also primarily builds closed models, but the company signed on in support of the open-weight letter after it was published, while Anthropic did not.
WATCH: Anthropic’s new AI model rivals Fable 5 and is cheaper as businesses fret about costs
Fireworks runs AI models for other businesses.

It specializes in open-weight models, which anyone can download, and helps customers tune them on their own data so they run faster and cheaper than the models of Anthropic, OpenAI, and other heavyweights, and are harder for rivals to copy.
Customers have included Uber, Shopify, and Notion.
Co-founder Chenyu Zhao and I spoke onstage toward the end of the day.
I describe Fireworks as a specialized intelligence platform.
OpenAI and Anthropic are building general intelligence.
That way you own your AI rather than being beholden to giant AI conglomerates.
If you’re just using Opus or Sonnet, that’s not a differentiator.

Zhao and many others believe companies are gravitating toward platforms like his because frontier models are pricey and, in most cases, he says, unnecessary unless you need the very latest and greatest generalized intelligence.
There’s one scenario in which it just continues to cement its place in this sort of oligopoly; there’s another where it starts to lose traction.

On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.

sources.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI company isn't advocating for ban of open-weight models - CNBC
passages: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said on Monday that his company has "never advocated for a ban on open-weights models," an attempt to beat back criticism emerging across the tech industry that the AI lab is trying to exert excessive control over the future of artificial intelligence.

Amodei published his views in a blog post on Monday, after a coalition of tech companies, including Nvidia , Microsoft , Meta and Palantir , released a letter late last week urging policymakers to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight models, which users can download, modify and run on their own infrastructure.
Chief rival OpenAI also primarily builds closed models, but the company signed on in support of the open-weight letter after it was published, while Anthropic did not.
